chunks: And set aside a portion of time for those with needs from you, wherein you free your person for them,
and sit for them in a general audience, so you humble yourself therein for Allah who created you,
and you keep away your army and your assistants from among your guards and police,
so that their speaker may speak to you without hesitation (or fear).

For I have heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say in more than one place: 'A nation will not achieve purity unless the right of the weak is taken from the strong without hesitation.'
ai.seo_question: What are the key administrative and ethical instructions for a governor in Nahj al-Balagha regarding public accessibility?
ai.summary: This directive from Imam Ali’s letter to Malik al-Ashtar underscores the Shia political ideal of *adl* (justice) through physical accessibility, where the ruler lowers himself to ensure the weak are heard without the hesitation (*muta'ta'ti'an*) caused by fear or status barriers. By citing the Prophet’s hadith, the Imam links administrative humility directly to the spiritual sanctity of the community, reflecting the Shi'a emphasis on the ruler as a servant of the people rather than a distant sovereign.
